facts.text: Yarmouth's historic village Main Street hosts homes from the 1700s, cafés, and shops, reflecting its shipbuilding past.
The Royal River’s Second, Third, and Fourth Falls line the town, offering scenic views just west of Bridge Street and near East Elm.
Yarmouth’s Riverside Cemetery, founded 1869, contains graves of early business owners like Leon Gorman and is listed on the National Register.
The Yarmouth History Center at 118 East Elm Street houses an interpretive gallery that traces the region from pre‑settlement to today.
In 1946, the Village Improvement Society preserved the interior of the historic meeting house, a gesture that continues to honor Yarmouth’s heritage.
Yarmouth’s railroad heritage includes two junctions—Royal Junction on Greely Road and Yarmouth Junction near Depot Road—once serving the Maine Central Railroad.
